description:
Searches for hotels by city, location or hotel ID. Not for restaurants, activities, car rentals or non-travel queries. Call places_find_location first: types=["city"] for a cityCode, types=["poi"] for coordinates, types=["hotel"] for a hotelId.

Each price is per night for all rooms in the search together. With 2 rooms, one price covers both rooms.

Polling flow:
1. Call without searchId. It returns a searchId at once (status "created", pollAgainInSeconds: 5).
2. Wait pollAgainInSeconds, then call with searchId. Status is "incomplete" (better rates still arriving) or "complete" (all providers answered).
3. While status is "incomplete", wait pollAgainInSeconds and call again. Stop at "complete". After 3 reads, use the results you have.
Once complete, every read (new filters, sorting or page) returns "complete" at once.

Use one search type per new search:
- citySearch: a city. For "near the airport" sort by "distance_from_nearest_airport_asc". For "downtown" sort by "distance_from_center_asc".
- geoSearch: a named airport, landmark or POI, sorted by "distance_asc". Radius 10km for a landmark, 20km for an airport, or the radius the user gives.
- hotelSearch: one hotel by ID.

Refinement: call with the searchId and new filters, sorting or pagination. Filters replace the previous filters entirely, so send again the ones to keep.

Filter options: a page 1 read with searchId returns filterOptions with the amenities, roomAmenities, brands, chains and propertyTypes of this search. Later pages do not. The lists are partial while status is "incomplete" and final at "complete". Each entry is { name, count }, where count is the approximate number of hotels in the whole search with that value, before filters. Amenity counts can be low. Each name is a valid value for the filter of the same name. Use these names in filters instead of guessing.

citySearch.description: Hotels in a city (e.g., 'hotels in Dubai' = {cityCode: 'DXB'}).

currencyCode.description: The currency the user pays in, as an ISO 4217 code (e.g. 'SAR', 'INR', 'USD'): the one they ask for, else the currency of their own country (siteCode). Do NOT take it from the destination: a user in India booking Dubai pays in 'INR'. Send the same code on every flight and hotel call in this conversation, searchId reads included.

filters.description: Filters to apply to search results.

amenities.description: Hotel property amenities — all must match (AND logic). Covers wifi, pool, parking, gym, spa, beach, restaurant, pet-friendly, etc. Short terms match best (e.g., 'wifi' not 'Free WiFi', 'pool' not 'Swimming Pool'). Fuzzy matching finds the closest match.

brands.description: Hotel brand names (OR logic). Short names match best (e.g., 'Holiday Inn' not 'Holiday Inn Express by IHG'). Fuzzy matching finds the closest match.

chains.description: Parent hotel chains/groups (OR logic). Short names match best (e.g., 'Marriott' not 'Marriott - Marriott Rewards'). When user says 'Hilton hotels', use chains, not brands.

priceRange.description: Budget filter on the price per night for all rooms together, in currencyCode. To filter on a per-room budget, multiply it by the number of rooms. For a total-stay budget, divide it by the number of nights. Examples: '2 rooms, under USD 50 for each room per night' = {max: 100}. 'USD 600 for 3 nights, 2 rooms' = {max: 200}.

max.description: Maximum price per night for all rooms together. A negative value becomes 0.

min.description: Minimum price per night for all rooms together. A negative value becomes 0.

propertyTypes.description: Accommodation type filter (e.g., 'resorts only' = ['Resort'], 'hotel or apartment' = ['Hotel', 'Apartment']). Short terms match best.

reviewScore.description: Guest satisfaction filter on 0-10 scale (e.g., 'highly rated' = {min: 8}).

max.description: Maximum guest review score (will be clamped to 0-10 range)

min.description: Minimum guest review score (will be clamped to 0-10 range)

roomAmenities.description: Room-level amenities — all must match (AND logic). Covers room-specific features like 'bathtub', 'balcony', 'minibar', 'kitchen', 'free cancellation'. NOT for property-wide facilities (wifi, pool, gym) — those go in amenities.

starRating.description: Hotel class filter (e.g., '4-star or above' = {min: 4}, '3 to 4 stars' = {min: 3, max: 4}).

max.description: Maximum star rating (will be clamped to 0-5 range)

min.description: Minimum star rating (will be clamped to 0-5 range)

geoSearch.description: Hotels near a location (e.g., 'near Eiffel Tower' = {latitude: 48.8584, longitude: 2.2945}). Use places_find_location for coordinates.

latitude.description: Latitude coordinate (will be clamped to -90 to 90 range)

longitude.description: Longitude coordinate (will be clamped to -180 to 180 range)

name.description: Name of the reference point for display (e.g., 'Burj Khalifa', 'Mall of the Emirates')

radius.description: Search radius in kilometers (minimum 10km enforced). Recommended values: 10km for city landmarks, 20km for airports, 30km for rural areas

hotelId.description: Hotel ID for single hotel search

page.description: Page number for pagination (will be clamped to minimum 1)

perPage.description: Number of results per page (will be clamped to 1-100 range)

rooms.description: Room config (e.g., [{adultsCount: 2, childrenCount: 1, childrenAges: [8]}]). REQUIRED when childrenCount > 0: ask for ages before searching.

adultsCount.description: Number of adults in the room (will be clamped to minimum 1)

childrenAges.description: Ages of each child (0-17). REQUIRED when childrenCount > 0 — if the user hasn't specified ages, ask them before searching. Do NOT guess or infer ages from other numbers like dates. Array format even for one child, e.g., [8] not 8.

childrenCount.description: Number of children in the room (will be clamped to minimum 0)

searchId.description: Reuse the searchId from a previous search when refining filters or sorting.

siteCode.description: The user's OWN country as an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code (e.g. 'SG', 'SA', 'IN'), when the conversation shows where the user is. It picks the Wego site that booking links open and the market prices come from. Do NOT take it from the departure, arrival or hotel city: a user in India searching London is still 'IN'. Omit it when unknown (default 'US'). Set it when the search is created; a searchId read keeps the search's site.

sorting.description: Sort order (e.g., 'cheapest first' = 'price_asc', 'closest to center' = 'distance_from_center_asc'). Default: relevance.
